- Overestimate early in the forecast horizon, especially after recent spikes; reduce initial forecast values by 5–10% if sentiment is neutral or negative.
- After a sharp price spike, model tends to overshoot; apply a downward correction of 5–15% for the first 3–5 days post-spike.
- When sentiment is consistently low or zero, model exhibits persistent overconfidence; apply a 3–7% mean-reversion bias toward historical 10-day average.
- Forecast horizon >14 days shows increasing underestimation of downward trends; adjust downward by 2–5% per 5-day segment for negative sentiment.
- If sentiment history includes a single positive value (e.g., 0.40), model may overreact; reduce forecast by 3–8% for the next 7 days unless sentiment persists.
- Avoid extrapolating recent volatility into future; if 3 consecutive days show high volatility, reduce forecast sensitivity by 20–30% for next 5 days.
